source.reference: Injection, access-control and server-side request classes from the OWASP Top Ten, reconstructed rather than copied

defect: The patch is spread over the existing profile, so any field a caller names is written: `{"role":"admin"}` makes the user an administrator and `{"email_verified":true}` marks an unverified address verified. Only `id` is protected, because only `id` was thought about. ac_2 asks for the edit to be restricted to the fields a user may change.
why_it_is_hard: The `id` override at the end of the spread is the tell that the author considered the problem, and it makes the line read as guarded. There is even a test asserting `id` cannot be changed, which is a true assertion about the one field that is safe and says nothing about the two that are not.
notes: Mass assignment with a partial guard and a test that certifies the guarded field. The test is honest and its subject is the wrong field.
